ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.19160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speaker diarization can drop people who speak only a little from its output entirely, and such losses barely affect the diarization error rate (DER), which measures the fraction of misattributed time. We examine Nemotron-3, an end-to-end diarization model with eight output slots, on 990 recordings from four corpora, and count lost speakers by how they were lost (overlap, merge, miss). ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.19280v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Beamforming has been widely recognized for its spatial filtering capability in speech signal processing, enabling effective interference rejection and signal enhancement. The performance of adaptive beamforming methods, e.g., the conventional minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming, often deteriorate significantly in complex and dynamic acoustic environments. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Pixel-KWS: Rendered-Glyph Representations for Orthographically Robust Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.19389v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting (KWS) allows users to enroll arbitrary keywords at inference time. However, character and phoneme-based text encoders rely on fixed symbol vocabularies learned during training, limiting their ability to handle unseen or visually similar symbols such as homoglyphs, l33tspeak substitutions, and accented characters. We propose PIXEL-KWS, an open-vocabulary KWS framework that represents characters through rendered glyphs rather than learned embedding lookups. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Leveraging Dual-Process Theory for Multimodal Multiparty Turn-Taking Prediction
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.19484v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In multiparty conversations, a pause does not always mean a speaker has finished, and another voice does not necessarily indicate a change in who holds the conversational floor. Reliable turn-taking therefore requires recognising not only whether a speaker is ready to yield the floor, but also when a possible transition deserves attention. We propose a dual-process-inspired framework that separates continuous candidate discovery from selective verification. A fast, recall-oriented stage identifies plausible transition points. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Rethinking Post-Training for Expressive Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.19787v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Zero-shot voice cloning typically emphasizes preserving the timbre and prosodic characteristics of a reference speaker. However, in real-world use, speech should adapt its delivery to the target text rather than remain tied to a fixed speaking style. In this work, we formulate this problem as text-adaptive prosody synthesis for zero-shot voice cloning and study how post-training can endow a cloning model with this capability. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: ProTTS: End-to-End Prominence-aware Natural and Controllable Text-to-Speech via Automatic Word Stress Discovery
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.19832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Natural speech conveys meaning not only through words, but also through the prominence on a few words. Yet most text-to-speech (TTS) systems remain prominence-unaware, existing prominence-aware TTS require external stress annotations, while unsupervised stress detectors operate in isolation, disconnected from synthesis. This creates a fundamental gap no existing system can automatically discover where stress should be placed, realize it as natural-sounding prosody, and offer user control over emphasis placement, all within a single model. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.20050v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Background: Before laryngoscopy, clinicians assess the likely cause of hoarseness and whether to suspect a precancerous or malignant lesion. Whether voice-based artificial intelligence (AI) supports pre-laryngoscopic categorization is unknown.

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.20254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continuous autoregressive TTS relies on an acoustic target that enables stable next-latent modeling while preserving fine-grained acoustic details. While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Validating Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion with Real-Time MRI: From Vocal-Tract Fidelity to Phonetic Consequences
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.20432v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Acoustic-to-articulatory inversion provides a promising way to estimate vocal-tract behaviour directly from speech, but inferred articulatory variables need to be validated against independent physical measurements before they can be interpreted as faithful estimates of articulation. We investigate this using paired real-time MRI (rtMRI) and speech. A WavLM-based inversion model is trained to predict eight vocal tract variables (TVs) extracted from rtMRI, achieving a mean correlation of 0.643 on held-out speakers. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.20630v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech foundation models pretrained via self-supervised learning provide powerful representations for deepfake detection, yet we find that standard fine-tuning exploits only the deepest transformer layers-leaving the majority of the network's capacity discriminatively inert. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.20954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Encoder-free audio-capable multimodal language models pro- vide a unique setting for studying how speech representations emerge inside a language-model decoder. In Gemma-4-12B, short waveform frames are projected directly into the shared embedding space, and all subsequent contextual processing is performed by the decoder layers. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.21140v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic voice disorder detection from speech offers strong potential for early diagnosis and continuous disease monitoring. While models based on pre-trained transformers have improved detection performance, their robustness to microphone variation remains underexplored, particularly for consumer-grade devices. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: OmniTag-LLM: Multilingual Multitask Speech Tagging
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.18589v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Multimodal LLMs promise to replace the traditional cascade of specialist speech models with a single system that, from one audio clip, jointly transcribes and labels emotion, gender, language, and named entities. Yet most benchmarks still score these tasks in isolation, and largely in English. We introduce OmniTag-Bench, a five-language benchmark (en/de/es/fr/it) and training recipe for joint understanding: one audio clip in, one JSON object out (transcript, emotion, gender, LID, token-level NER). ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.18653v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: For a low-resource language, one public leaderboard is often the only shared measure of progress, so optimizing toward it means optimizing toward a test distribution. arXiv:2611.18924v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Supervisory control of multiple autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) imposes high visual and cognitive demands on human operators, particularly when communicating mission objectives and system constraints. Voice command provides a natural interaction modality that can reduce operator workload; however, its reliability is affected by environmental noise, speech variability, and recognition errors. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.19223v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study zero-shot fine-grained singing technique conversion (STC), which applies specified techniques to selected regions of an existing singing recording while preserving lyrics, melody, timing, and singer identity. Existing singing conversion and synthesis methods offer complementary strengths in source preservation and explicit technique control, but combining both in an audio-to-audio setting remains underexplored, especially with limited technique-annotated data. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.19236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio-visual representation learning commonly aligns paired audio and visual signals with sample-level contrastive objectives. However, real-world audio-visual pairs usually contain heterogeneous patch tokens: only a subset carries reliable cross-modal shared semantics, while many others mainly encode modality-private residuals. Aggregating all tokens into a single global representation can therefore introduce semantic noise into cross-modal alignment. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.19260v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conventional text-to-speech (TTS) systems can lose intelligibility in noise environments because they cannot adapt to environmental changes. However, humans tend to increase their vocal efforts in noisy environments, a phenomenon known as the Lombard effect. Building on an auditory-feedback Lombard TTS, we investigate whether a pretrained Flow-based TTS can learn acoustic adaptation directly from auditory feedback without explicit prosodic control. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.19706v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent generative speech separation methods have shown promising performance, yet mixtures of overlapping speech in different languages remain underexplored. To this end, we first curate MuSSeD, an English-Korean benchmark comprising two- to four- speaker mixtures across varying overlap ratios. We further propose MOUSSE, a flow matching framework that incorporates boundary-aware training and frame-wise predictive uncertainty through a permutation-invariant Gaussian negative log-likelihood. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.19714v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.19844v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Target-speaker automatic speech recognition (TS-ASR) is essential for reliable human-machine interaction in complex acoustic environments, where overlapping speech and background noise make it difficult to identify and recognize the intended speaker. Existing approaches typically rely on speaker enrollment or cascaded processing pipelines, limiting their flexibility in practical applications. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.20436v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech language models (SLMs) exhibit strong capabilities in automatic speech recognition (ASR) and general-purpose speech understanding, yet ASR-specific training often degrades spoken question answering (QA) performance. We revisit this conflict from the perspective of task-specific input--output mappings and one-hot supervision. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.20725v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio Moment Retrieval (AMR) aims to locate the temporal segment within a long audio recording that semantically corresponds to a natural-language query. This task is particularly challenging because query-related audio events are often sparsely distributed and embedded in complex acoustic environments, where background sounds and acoustically similar events can easily obscure the target moments. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Surprise-Gated Memory for Live Speaker Diarization
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.20819v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We transpose the Surprise-Gated Memory recipe, a frozen encoder plus a calibrated novelty signal that gates a one-shot episodic store consolidated by periodic replay, from continual visual learning to live speaker diarization. The moment-to-moment question a streaming diarizer must answer, whether an arriving voice belongs to an already-heard speaker or a new one, is a known-versus-novel decision, exactly the decision the surprise gate is built for. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.20822v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gender expansive voices remain underrepresented in speech datasets, which could cause challenges with generalizability in zero-shot Text-To-Speech (TTS) systems. We evaluate six zero-shot TTS models on two datasets: one containing non gender expansive voices (N-GE) and one with gender expansive (GE) voices from self-identified speakers. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Think2Listen: Evidence-Centric Learning For Agentic Audio Understanding With LALMS
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.21083v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large audio-language models (LALMs) have broadened audio understanding across speech, sound, and music, with tool-based agents further supporting these tasks by invoking predefined audio tools. However, a persistent gap remains between perceiving acoustic content and using it as evidence for reasoning: recognizing what is audible does not ensure that a model can identify which cues resolve an uncertain decision. To bridge this gap, we propose Think2Listen, an evidence-centric learning framework for agentic audio understanding.

CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Berlin Kraftwerk, the former power plant in Berlin Mitte associated with Tresor and Atonal Festival, was the venue last week for Helsing's launch of new agentic technology, Clarity. This platform uses the same controversial AI-driven approach implicated in accelerating the use of flawed intelligence and killing civilians in Palestine, Lebanon, and Iran. Kraftwerk's Head of Sales has taken sole responsibility and apologized. But the fiasco seems emblematic of Berlin's pivot from cultural capital to military-industrial capital, with the money that follows.

CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The masterful artist Ryo Fujimoto works in electronics not just as a passive actor behind machines, but fully embodied in physicality, voice, and sometimes screams. He sends his latest live performance -- an arresting, but ultimately healing performance that takes on war and violence in a powerful machine-vocal cry.

Guitars are reimagined as koi ponds. Sounds get transformed into wearable resin structures. It's enough to make you want to up your airbrush, math, and science games.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Ableton Live 13 hands-on: ARA 2, Drum Synth, new effects, more
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Ableton Live 13 is now in limited public beta. That includes a lot of what you've asked for, like multi-band Racks, overhauled preset navigation, and ARA 2 support for tools like Melodyne. And it's packed with new goodies: a very Ableton step sequencer, a multi-engine Drum Synth with some nice twists, new effects, a new ambient looper, and more. Also, I know some of you will like this: no mention of AI. It's like we just get to talk about music-making tools again.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: There’s a Zelda-friendly ocarina app for FM-1, and you can try it in a browser
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Now Ocarina of Time meets up with the other big trend of the fall, with OCA, an ocarina app and soundbook for the M-VAVE FM-1. You don't even need an FM-1 to play with it; it runs perfectly in a browser, including on a phone. Developer Charles Vestal gives us a look.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Mods for everyone: inMusic is opening up MPC, more new gear to coders
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
You may have seen Akai tease an “open-source” MPC keyboard running vibe-coded mods. But there’s more coming—a lot more. inMusic, parent of Moog, Akai, Numark, Alesis, Denon, and others, promises that many of its 22 product launches coming in January will be open to modders and developer. That suggests a sweeping change in approach for […]

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Productions gone live, as Jlin joins Third Coast Percussion on “Vernacular”
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
If today is a day to celebrate good things happening in the USA, you better also be listening to the epic collaboration between Jlin and Chicago's Third Coast Percussion. That puts the Gary, Indiana-born Jerrilynn Patton (Jlin) right up alongside Philip Glass and David Longstreth, where frankly, she totally belongs. And it's touring.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Mixxx could unlock free and open standalone DJing — but, like, stable
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Daniel Schürmann of the long-running libre/free DJ software project Mixxx has a compelling proposal for uniting efforts to develop their DJ software on embedded hardware, from emerging cheap "open" hardware to DIY projects. It could mean a chance for openness to have a moment -- while avoiding the chaotic slop of countless separate forks and hacks.
